edges.effect_quant: The strongest quantitative studies point in a protective direction, but the pooled magnitude varies across populations and methods.
edges.mechanism: Acceptance and commitment therapy plausibly improves depression through a factor-specific pathway documented in the literature, even if the exact size of benefit varies by population and dose.
edges.summary: What makes this pair believable is not one flashy paper but the way the literature stacks up: the 2026 Carrier meta analysis in Neuropsychol Rehabil already points to acceptance and commitment therapy tracks with lower risk or better outcomes, and later studies mostly refine the size of the effect rather than overturning it. In practice this reads more like a real risk signal than a one-off finding.
edges.caveats: Healthier-user bias, screening intensity, and baseline risk can all inflate apparent benefit in observational work, so the magnitude should be read conservatively.
